abstract.p: While deep neural networks (DNNs) excel in computer vision tasks, their real-world deployment is hindered by robustness limitations compared to human perception. Adversarial attacks and data distribution shifts remain critical vulnerabilities, degrading model performance under practical conditions. To address these challenges and advance robustness research, we introduce a comprehensive, userfriendly toolkit for training, evaluating, and analyzing robust vision models. It targets two key dimensions of robustness: 1) Adversarial robustness-defending against malicious worst-case perturbations (adversarial examples); 2) Natural robustness-maintaining performance under real-world corruptions and distribution shifts. Through extensive image classification benchmarks, our toolkit enables precise model assessment. We envision this toolkit accelerating the development of practically robust models and bridging the gap between machine and human vision capabilities.
